newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz won't rule out Ergo withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: Allianz won't rule out Ergo withdrawal.

text.p: German insurer Allianz AG said on Thursday that it would not rule out withdrawing from the Ergo mega-merger announced last week.

Allianz owns about 10 percent of Ergo as a result of its 20 percent stake in Hanburg-Mannheimer, a unit of rival Munich Re. Munich Re formed Ergo by merging its DKV and Hamburger-Mannnheimer with Victoria Holding AG.
The company has not yet decided what to do with its Ergo stake and it has "not fully ruled out" pulling out of the venture, chief executive Henning Schulte-Noelle said at the firm's annual meeting.

Allianz had no plans to change its holding in Munich Re in the wake of the Ergo merger, he added. Munich Re, which was expected to have a majority share in Ergo, is a traditional ally of Allianz and each company owns 25 percent of the other.
Schulte-Noelle also said its market position as Germany's largest insurer would not be threatened by Ergo, which would become the nation's second largest insurance comapny.
"We look forward to the competition and go into the competition relatively confident," he said.
Earlier on Thursday, Allianz said it expected to raise its return on equity after tax to 15 percent from 11.5 percent in the medium term and forecast a small double-digit rise in 1997 earnings.
